messages:
Alex Cheng: CI microbench failed on merged PR 18385, threshold diff 22% tail latency. ci-bot reported metric: "batch_latency_p95: baseline=48.2ms, head=58.8ms" :cry:
ci-bot: FAILURE: pr/18385 microbench (seq=256, batch=auto) - p95 latency increased by 22% (48.2ms -> 58.8ms). Full report: https://ci.redwood.example/archived/18385/report.html
Maria Gomez: hmm that delta is big. which microbench exactly?
Alex Cheng: the continuous-batcher microbench. config attached in CI log. KV hit rate flat (~93-95%) so not cache missy.
Devon Liu: linking the PR that landed yesterday: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/18385 (reordered kernel registry + small timer tweak)
Samir Patel: @Devon can you bisect locally? I suspect the kernel registry reorder caused the autoselect to prefer a different matmul kernel on Ampere which regresses latency under this async-batching shape.
Devon Liu: starting quick bisect. repro on an ampere instance with same image. running the microbench with pinned seed.
Olivia Ng: FYI infra telemetry shows a short window of GPU power capping on some hosts around the same time as the CI runs. Could be noisy infra too. logs: s3://redwood-telemetry/gpu-telemetry/2026/03/08
Alex Cheng: good call. but local reproduces even on my workstation so not purely infra. Devon, do you see kernel name switches in the trace?
Devon Liu: yes. with main (pre-PR) autoselect picks kernel "matmul_v1_fused". with HEAD it picks "matmul_v3_sparseopt". p95 moves from ~48ms -> ~58ms.
Samir Patel: that matches autotuner weight drift. we changed kernel registration order which changed the deterministic tie-breaker in selection. not ideal.
Maria Gomez: can we force old kernel temporarily in CI? maybe REDWOOD_FORCE_KERNEL=matmul_v1_fused to validate hypothesis.
Devon Liu: trying that now locally:

# quick repro
export REDWOOD_FORCE_KERNEL=matmul_v1_fused
make microbench RUN_OPTS="--seq 256 --iters 200 --batcher=continuous"

Devon Liu: with forced kernel p95 back to 49.1ms, matches baseline margin.
Alex Cheng: good repro. so two potential fixes: revert the registry reorder (safe, predictable) or change autoselect to prefer by explicit perf table rather than registration order.
Olivia Ng: rollout status: the PR was part of last night's small rollout group (canary=10%). We should pause further rollout until fix.
Samir Patel: agree. I'll open a revert PR for the registry change (refs abc123). Also filing an issue to make kernel autoselect stable (bug 2026-112).
Maria Gomez: also add a CI guard that runs a small microbench after merge to catch p95 regressions >10% on canary nodes.
ci-bot: created ticket #2026-112: "stabilize kernel autoselect tie-breaker" and opened revert PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/18401
Alex Cheng: nice. Devon, once revert is up can you run a quick CI-run to confirm metrics return to baseline?
Devon Liu: kicked off a CI job against revert-branch. will paste results.
ci-bot: CI job started: https://ci.redwood.example/job/18401/1
Devon Liu: job finished: microbench p95=49.0ms, threshold diff -1.5% (within noise).
Alex Cheng: OK hold rollout, merge revert. follow-up: change autoselect to consult per-hardware perf table and include a tie-breaker seed to avoid regressing on innocuous reorderings.
Samir Patel: opened a PR for autoselect change draft (WIP) and added unit tests for selection determinism.
Olivia Ng: adding infra note to monitor GPU power capping windows too, just in case.
Maria Gomez: thanks all. post-mortem item: add a small microbench to post-merge smoke for canaries. :thumbsup:
Alex Cheng: agreed. closing thread once revert merged. :eyes:
Devon Liu: revert merged (18401) and rollout paused.
Alex Cheng: closing — thanks everyone.
